newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bankers to buy Crown Leasing's overseas portfolios.
newsitem.headline: Bankers to buy Crown Leasing's overseas portfolios.

text.p: The Tokyo branch of Bankers Trust said on Friday it had decided to buy the overseas financial portfolios of Crown Leasing Corp, one of the three financial affiliates of Nippon Credit Bank which went bankrupt in April.
Bankers Trust would not disclose the price or the extact timing of the transaction, but said they aim to complete the deal by June or July.
"According to the liquidator's estimate, the book value of the portfolios held by Crown Leasing total 75 billion yen," a Bankers Trust official said.
He told Reuters that the portfolios include loans, and bonds such as U.S. Treasury bonds, European government bonds and U.S and European corporate bonds.

In April, Nippon Credit Bank (NCB) announced a drastic restructuring programme which included a withdrawal from overseas operations and an increase in its capital by issuing new equities to other banks and insurance companies.
It also signed a business agreement with Bankers Trust to securitise its real estate and other assets.
The official, however, said that the decision to purchase the overseas portofolio of Crown Leasing had nothing to do with the business agreement with NCB.
"People tend to link NCB and us with this deal (with Crown Leasing), but NCB has nothing to do with it," the official said. "We reached this decision through the process of the liquidator."
